findings.problem: The image column has no fixed width and is not aligned. ci-job and notes images sit at different x positions than api and agent-1, and the specs and Updated columns also drift. The list reads as ragged floating text rather than a table. There are no column headers.
findings.fix: Use a real grid with fixed columns (name+state, image, specs, updated, actions) and column headers. Truncate long image names with an ellipsis and a tooltip.

findings.location: Row actions: Open terminal, Stop, VS Code
findings.problem: Every running row has a filled cyan primary button, so four rows give four competing accent blocks. Row buttons are as loud as the page's New workspace CTA. The accent stops meaning one primary action per view. Stop is an outline with the same weight as View logs, so a destructive-ish action is not distinguished from navigation.
findings.fix: Make row actions quiet: ghost or outline buttons, with the accent reserved for New workspace. Put Stop and Delete behind a row menu, or give them a danger-tinted hover state.

findings.location: Header icon buttons and the filter bar
findings.problem: The state counts (Running 2, Stopped 1, Failed 1) look like passive labels and not filters. They have no selected state or button affordance. The 'waiting' state is missing from the summary. The search input has the same weight as the rows.
findings.fix: Make the counts toggle chips with active and hover states, and add a waiting count. Give the search field a distinct inset surface.

findings.problem: State is a 6px dot or square plus small mono text. In c01 the stopped ring is the same grey as the body text and the failed pink is faint. The shapes are tiny and read as decoration. In c05 the dimmed state colours lose contrast. The waiting diamond never appears in the app list, only in c09.
findings.fix: Enlarge the markers to about 8–10px and set the state label in a medium-weight small-caps style. Use the same four shape-and-colour pairs in every screen, including the app list.

findings.location: Overview page: Details and Resources tables, Connect card
findings.problem: The key/value tables and the Connect card all use the same hairline-and-outline treatment, so contextual detail, content and operations sit at the same level. The Connect card is a bordered box containing another box, which is nested chrome. The tab strip, tables and card have nearly equal weight, and a lot of empty space is left below.
findings.fix: Move Connect into a flat, code-only block with a copy affordance. Drop the nested border. Give section headings a stronger style, and put the status and metrics (CPU and memory use) in a summary band under the title.

findings.location: Header: api title and action buttons
findings.problem: The title is small for a page title. The state, image and actions float on different baselines. VS Code is a bare text link with no affordance, and the Delete action is absent from the detail page, so the destructive action is hidden.
findings.fix: Align the actions on one baseline. Give VS Code a ghost button style. Put Delete in a separated danger zone or a '…' menu in the header.

findings.problem: The dialog is a good model: red Delete, typed confirmation, inline error. But the Delete button is enabled while the typed name does not match. The destructive red (#C2304F) sits close to the failed pink, so 'failed' and 'destructive' share a hue family. The dialog surface barely separates from the dimmed page.
findings.fix: Disable Delete until the name matches. Separate the destructive red from the failed colour (a deeper red against a lighter pink-red). Give the dialog a stronger elevation or border.

findings.problem: The sidebar is gone, with no menu button or navigation visible. The running rows have a full-width cyan block that takes more room than the name. The failed row has no action, and the stopped row has a different button than the running ones. The image, specs and Updated columns are dropped, so the list loses most of its data.
findings.fix: Design a compact card per row: name and state, then the image in mono, then a quiet action. Add a top bar with a menu button. Keep a Stop/Open overflow menu on every row.

findings.problem: The hero headline is set in huge mono at around 56px with wide letter-spacing, so it reads as a poster and breaks awkwardly at 'per / workspace'. Meanwhile the glossy 3D logo illustration is stylistically alien to the flat, restrained UI. The site is framed inside a rounded bordered 'device' box with a 'THE SITE' label above it, which is lab-page chrome.
findings.fix: Use a mono face only for short labels and code, and a proportional display face at lower weight for the headline. Replace the glossy mark with a flat or simplified version used consistently in the app.

findings.location: Docs table and callout at the bottom of the article
findings.problem: The comparison table sits directly below the Caution callout with almost no space. It has no border or header treatment beyond a thin rule. The code blocks use the same surface as the caution, so a code block and a warning are hard to tell apart. The callout only has a thin amber left rule.
findings.fix: Add 24px of space above the table. Give the table a header row on a tinted surface. Give the caution a distinct amber-tinted surface and a text label.

findings.location: Dashboard lab: toast and dialog placement
findings.problem: The dialog and toast sit inline under the table as bordered boxes, so the page shows two unrelated systems. The table here has a Host and a Last snapshot column and underlined link names, which the app list (c01) does not use. The Delete/Cancel button order is reversed relative to c05. The list differs between c01 and c09 (names as underlined links versus bold text).
findings.fix: Make c09 and the app list one component. Pick a single order (Cancel left, Delete right) and one name style.

findings.problem: The palette is a navy-slate surface stack (#111827, #172035, #202C47, #273552) with a saturated cyan (#27BFE8) and a saturated teal-mint label colour. The four surfaces are one hue and differ only slightly, so cards and page blur together. Hard-saturated green, amber and pink on navy look neon and generic-dashboard. The accent-text equals the accent. The success mint and the label teal are almost the same colour, so accent and success collide.
findings.fix: Widen the lightness steps between surfaces or lean on borders. Lower the saturation of the state colours, and move the label colour to a neutral. Keep cyan for actions only and give the success green a different hue.

findings.problem: The light theme is a straight inversion: white page, white sidebar, a pale blue-grey selected nav item that is nearly invisible. The fills of the filled primary buttons (dark teal-blue) are darker and heavier than in dark mode, and the four of them dominate the list. The thin grey hairlines are nearly all the structure there is.
findings.fix: Give the light theme its own surface ladder: a tinted page and white raised rows, plus a clearly tinted sidebar and a visible selected-item treatment. Reduce the row buttons to quiet outlines.

findings.problem: The code block is a saturated pale blue-grey slab that is the strongest fill on the page. The 'Change' link inside the Network value, the URL link and the Open terminal button all use the same blue, so links and primary actions blur together.
findings.fix: Use a neutral light grey for code. Distinguish links by underline and a different weight from filled buttons.

findings.location: Light-mode dashboard lab at mobile width
findings.problem: The table squeezes into a narrow width: the Last snapshot header wraps, host chips wrap mid-word (runner- / a1), and agent-1 wraps with a hyphen break. The waiting state wraps over three lines. The dialog floats over the table and covers it with a heavy shadow.
findings.fix: At narrow widths, stack each row as a card: name and state on one line, host in mono on the next, and keep ids unbroken (white-space: nowrap or a smaller chip). Dock the dialog as a bottom sheet.

findings.problem: The lab page is a long, flat sequence of swatches with the same card treatment for everything. It does not show contrast ratios, the light palette in the same view, or the type scale. Swatch labels are very small, low-contrast mono.
findings.fix: Show each pair with its contrast ratio and a pass/fail mark, show the light and dark values side by side, and add a type specimen with the scale.

findings.problem: Rows are not a table. Image, resources and 'Updated' float at different x-positions on each row, because the columns are sized to their content. Row actions also change by state: Open terminal, Stop and VS Code on running rows, View logs on failed, Start on stopped. Scanning a column is impossible.
findings.fix: Use fixed grid columns: name, state, image, resources, updated, actions. Right-align the actions and give every row the same action slots.

findings.location: Every running row: Open terminal button
findings.problem: The bright cyan filled button repeats on every running row, plus New workspace and Start. Accent-filled buttons dominate the page and compete with the state colours. The brand's own rule is one primary action per view.
findings.fix: Make row actions neutral outline or ghost buttons. Keep the filled accent for New workspace only, or for the single primary action in a detail view.

findings.problem: State is a 12px monospace word next to a tiny dot. It is easy to miss and dims further in the dark theme. The waiting state (amber diamond) appears in c09 but not in the list. The filter chips (Running 2, Stopped 1) look like plain text, not controls.
findings.fix: Add a fixed-width State column with a larger glyph plus label. Show the waiting state in the list. Draw the filters as real segmented chips with a selected state.

findings.location: Page chrome, top-right toolbar and sidebar
findings.problem: Two unlabeled square icon buttons sit next to the CTA. The sidebar is flat and has no sections, and the content area is mostly empty. The screen reads as generic SaaS next to Beam and boxd, which have breadcrumbs, org context and resource meters.
findings.fix: Label or tooltip the toolbar buttons. Group the nav into sections. Add useful context to the sidebar and header, such as a host or quota summary.

findings.problem: The label/value tables have hairlines only and no scale for values. The Connect card is a box inside a box, and its code block uses a barely different fill. The tab bar (Access, Status, History, Snapshots...) has little weight, and the open tab is marked by only a thin underline. The state is shown only in small text under the title.
findings.fix: Put a state badge beside the title. Use one surface level per container. Strengthen the active tab. Add a copy affordance to the command block.

findings.location: Header actions: Open terminal / Stop / VS Code
findings.problem: Stop and Change size are neutral outlines, so a destructive or disruptive action does not look different from the safe ones. VS Code is a bare text link that looks like a different component. There is no Delete or Snapshot action in the detail header.
findings.fix: Make the three actions one consistent button group. Move Delete into a separated danger zone or a menu, in the destructive red.

findings.problem: The dialog is clear and the red Delete is distinct. But Delete is enabled while the typed name does not match. The pink error text is small and low in contrast. Cancel and Delete are packed tightly, with Cancel placed before the red button. The scrim is light enough that the list behind it stays loud.
findings.fix: Disable Delete until the name matches. Use a larger error message with an icon. Darken the scrim. Put the destructive action at a consistent position.

findings.problem: The scrim turns the light page grey-blue and the dialog is plain white with a hairline. Pink and magenta error text on white is weak. The list behind it is still fully readable and visually competes.
findings.fix: Use a stronger scrim and an elevated dialog shadow. Check the error-text contrast on white.

findings.problem: Narrow layout drops image, resources and updated time entirely. Running rows show only a huge Open terminal button, and the failed row has no action. Two oversized cyan buttons dominate. The icon buttons, search and New workspace are stacked with no navigation visible and no way to open the menu.
findings.fix: Design a compact card or row with state, name, image and one overflow menu. Add a mobile top bar with a menu button. Keep only one accent button on the page.

findings.location: Docs site: hero and code blocks
findings.problem: The hero heading is a very large monospace face. At display size it is wide and loose, so it reads as a gimmick and wraps awkwardly. Code blocks, the output block and the Caution callout all use the same raised fill, and the table beneath has no borders, so the page is a stack of equally weighted boxes. The caution left stripe is yellow in dark and brown in light.
findings.fix: Set the headline in the proportional face with tighter tracking and keep mono for ids and commands. Differentiate code, output and callout by border or tint. Give the table a defined header.

findings.location: Docs site: eyebrow labels and shell
findings.problem: The mint monospaced uppercase labels (THE SITE, ON THIS PAGE, SPIN-STACK) are a different green from the success state, so the label colour clashes with the state semantics. The embedded site frame has a rounded border that the product does not use. The hero illustration is glossy and photographic against an otherwise flat UI.
findings.fix: Put labels in the muted text colour or in the accent colour. Drop the frame rounding. Flatten the illustration or tone it to the palette.

findings.problem: This table has real columns, with Name, State, Host and Last snapshot. It contradicts the actual app list in c01, which has no columns, and the nav labels differ (Work/Administer here, flat in c01). Names are underlined links in cyan, so the page is cluttered with underlines. This component shows the waiting state, but the app does not.
findings.fix: Bring the app to this structure and use one list pattern. Use an unlined link style that shows on hover and state-coloured rows.

findings.location: Delete dialog and toast placed inline
findings.problem: The dialog and the toast sit directly beneath the table as static boxes. Cancel comes after Delete here but before it in c05. The toast has a mint left stripe and a monospaced message, so it looks like an error block.
findings.fix: Show components in context. Fix the order of Cancel and Delete everywhere.

findings.problem: Surfaces page, surface, raised and overlay differ by only a few lightness points on a navy base, so nested cards blend into one navy. Muted text #9AA9C2 is the only secondary tone, and it is used for many small labels. Border #33435F is faint. The accent cyan, the label mint, the success green and the selected teal are four close hues in the green-blue range. Pink for failure and the saturated red for destructive are close but different.
findings.fix: Widen the surface steps and strengthen the border. Reserve cyan for actions and links only. Choose one distinct hue per state. Check the muted-on-surface contrast for small text.

findings.problem: The app uses a small body size (about 11-12px) for nearly everything: metadata, buttons, tabs, labels. Row names at 12px bold are barely above the metadata, and the mono ids and images are at 12-13px in grey. The title is 20px. There is little hierarchy between sections.
findings.fix: Raise body to 13-14px. Set names at 14px semi-bold and image ids at the same size in mono. Use three clear text tiers.

findings.problem: Light mode is competent but flat: a white page, a light-grey sidebar, and a pale blue-grey code fill with a solid dark-blue accent button. The selected nav item is nearly invisible. The identity is generic and it lacks a point of view.
findings.fix: Strengthen the selected nav state with an accent bar. Give light mode its own surface ladder rather than a copy of the dark one.

findings.location: Workspace list rows and surrounding canvas
findings.problem: The table occupies a shallow strip at the top while the rest of the desktop canvas is empty, making an operational inventory feel under-utilized and reducing scan momentum.
findings.fix: Constrain the workspace area to a deliberate content width and add meaningful adjacent or below-table operational context, or increase row density and provide a clear empty lower-state boundary rather than an unbounded canvas.

findings.problem: Rows have no visible column labels; image, resource, recency, and actions must be inferred from alignment alone.
findings.fix: Add a compact table header with muted labels and retain it while scanning longer lists.

findings.problem: The sidebar is visually strong but its active blue surface is close to the main dark surface, while thin borders carry most separation.
findings.fix: Increase surface separation slightly between navigation, page, and selected navigation state; preserve the restrained palette but make hierarchy less dependent on hairlines.

findings.problem: Light mode inherits cool blue-gray borders and fills nearly everywhere, which makes the page feel washed out and gives secondary structure similar weight to content.
findings.fix: Use a warmer or more neutral page surface, reserve blue-gray fills for controls and code, and reduce border prominence for ordinary row separation.

findings.problem: The two-column data groups lack a stronger section-level distinction from the large Connect panel, so the lower panel competes with primary workspace facts.
findings.fix: Tighten the Connect panel or give it a subtler treatment; establish a clearer heading-to-data rhythm for the two operational summary columns.

findings.problem: Inline action text such as “Change” and the long Saved sentence read as a continuous data value, weakening scannability.
findings.fix: Style inline actions distinctly and constrain/structure verbose status values so labels, facts, and actions remain separable.

findings.problem: The dark modal blends closely with the dark app surface, while the backdrop is extremely dark; the destructive decision lacks a sufficiently isolated focal plane.
findings.fix: Raise the modal surface and shadow separation, and tune the overlay so the dialog is unmistakably foreground without obscuring all contextual evidence.

findings.problem: Light and dark dialogs use materially different perceived elevation: the light dialog has a strong shadow and bright plane, while dark mode has weak plane separation.
findings.fix: Define matched elevation tokens for both themes—surface contrast, border, backdrop, and shadow—so modal hierarchy is equivalent.

findings.problem: Mobile removes image, resource, updated time, Stop, VS Code, and View logs without exposing an overflow action or disclosure path; key workflows are lost.
findings.fix: Use expandable rows or a per-row overflow menu containing the omitted metadata and actions, with a compact state-first summary.

findings.problem: The action controls wrap into an ambiguous three-item cluster before the search and state filters, obscuring their purpose and weakening the scan order.
findings.fix: Make New workspace the clear first-row primary action and place secondary global controls in a labeled overflow or a separate toolbar.

findings.location: Documentation site shell and content panes
findings.problem: Multiple near-identical navy surfaces, borders, and boxed code/callout treatments create a dense enclosed feel; navigation, article, and contextual TOC do not separate enough by surface role.
findings.fix: Reduce container borders, use fewer elevated surfaces, and establish clearer base/raised/code/callout roles while keeping the dark technical aesthetic.

findings.problem: Several body and secondary-text tones are light enough to be readable but subdued against the expansive white canvas, especially in side navigation and explanatory copy.
findings.fix: Increase secondary-text contrast and use less blue-gray tint for normal prose; reserve muted tones for genuinely secondary metadata.

findings.problem: The delete panel is embedded below the table rather than presented as a confirmation dialog and lacks the typed-name safeguard visible in the app flow.
findings.fix: Use the same destructive confirmation pattern across product surfaces, including explicit target confirmation and a foreground modal or anchored confirmation state.

findings.problem: The four-column table is forced into a narrow card, causing state and host labels to wrap awkwardly and damaging quick operational scanning.
findings.fix: Transform each workspace into a stacked compact row on narrow screens, prioritizing name, state, host, recency, and an action menu.

findings.problem: The palette names and swatches are clear, but the oversized rigid matrix leaves the semantic relationship between tokens and applied UI states mostly abstract.
findings.fix: Add small paired component specimens for each surface/action/state token, especially light-mode applications and contrast-critical text combinations.

findings.problem: The entire operational interface is rendered at a very small type size, including statuses, resource facts, timestamps, and button labels. This weakens scanability and makes the wide empty canvas feel underused.
findings.fix: Increase the base UI/data text scale and row height modestly; retain compactness through clearer column widths and reduced unused page area rather than tiny text.

findings.problem: Primary terminal actions, secondary stop actions, and the quiet VS Code link are tightly packed into the same visual band, while row metadata has little hierarchy.
findings.fix: Establish a consistent action area: primary terminal button first, compact secondary actions, then integration link; use stronger alignment and separation from resource metadata.

findings.problem: The detail page leaves a large gap between the workspace identity and its tabs, so the relationship between identity, operational controls, and section navigation is weaker than it should be.
findings.fix: Treat the identity block, status, primary actions, and tabs as one compact header region with a shared alignment rhythm.

findings.problem: The two data groups use faint, repeated horizontal rules and low-emphasis labels that make the information feel visually flat, especially in dark mode.
findings.fix: Use fewer but more intentional dividers, slightly stronger label/value contrast, and a shared definition-list grid; reserve stronger borders for section boundaries.

findings.problem: The destructive confirmation is shown against an extremely subtle dark overlay, leaving the background almost as prominent as the dialog and reducing focus on the irreversible task.
findings.fix: Use a substantially darker, neutral scrim and preserve a clearly elevated modal surface with a focused shadow and border.

findings.problem: The destructive action appears available despite a visible name mismatch; the confirmation control does not clearly communicate its disabled/error-dependent state.
findings.fix: Disable Delete until the exact name matches, with a visibly disabled treatment; enable it only after valid input while retaining the inline validation copy.

findings.location: Delete confirmation dialog in light mode
findings.problem: Light mode uses a gray-blue backdrop and cool shadow that make the dialog feel washed out rather than intentionally elevated; it differs materially from the dark-mode surface logic.
findings.fix: Define modal elevation tokens for both themes: neutral scrim, dedicated raised surface, consistent border contrast, and restrained shadow.

findings.problem: Responsive behavior removes image, resource, timestamp, stop, VS Code, and log actions without offering a clear route to the omitted operational controls.
findings.fix: Turn each row into a compact disclosure/card pattern: preserve status and primary action, and expose metadata plus secondary actions through a row menu or expanded detail.

findings.problem: The two unlabeled icon-placeholder controls sit detached above the primary action and consume scarce vertical space.
findings.fix: Group utility controls with the primary action in a compact toolbar, or move lower-priority controls into an overflow menu.

findings.problem: The marketing documentation shell is visually much more stylized and spacious than the product console, making the brand feel like two related but separate systems.
findings.fix: Share a core type scale, surface/border tokens, action shapes, and navigation density between docs and product while preserving the documentation layout.

findings.problem: The outer frame, three-column body, internal section borders, code blocks, and caution block create many simultaneous rectangular boundaries.
findings.fix: Reduce redundant container borders and let spacing establish most hierarchy; keep borders for navigation separation, code, and high-priority callouts.

findings.problem: The confirmation appears as an inline card below the table rather than a clearly scoped modal or row-level workflow, which makes the affected workspace and action state ambiguous.
findings.fix: Use a modal confirmation for destructive deletion, or attach an inline confirmation directly to the selected row with an explicit selected state.

findings.problem: The four-column table is retained at a width too narrow for state and host values, causing awkward wrapping and unstable row rhythm.
findings.fix: Transform the table into stacked workspace summaries on narrow screens, with host and snapshot facts as secondary lines and actions in a footer.

findings.problem: Several palette swatches and the page presentation rely on similar blue-gray surfaces, while labels and explanatory copy are comparatively muted; the system does not clearly demonstrate robust semantic and elevation separation.
findings.fix: Document and apply stricter contrast-tested tokens for page, surface, raised, overlay, border, muted text, and semantic states; show representative component pairings in both themes.

findings.problem: Navigation selection, primary actions, documentation links, hover-like blue surfaces, and cyan accent all occupy closely related blue/cyan territory, diluting the accent's operational meaning.
findings.fix: Reserve the bright accent for primary actions and links, use a quieter selected-navigation token, and keep state colors exclusive to their semantic statuses.

Demote row-level operational actions ('Open terminal', 'Start') to secondary outline or ghost buttons, reserving the solid #27BFE8 accent fill exclusively for the view's single primary CTA ('New workspace').
findings.problem: Accent overuse and broken action hierarchy: Every running row displays a solid, bright cyan (#27BFE8) primary button for 'Open terminal', identical in styling and visual weight to the top-level 'New workspace' CTA. This floods the view with competing primary actions, violating the principle of one primary action per view.

findings.fix: Replace row flexbox with a structured grid or table layout having fixed column widths and clear column headers (Name, Image, Specs, Updated, Actions) so metadata aligns vertically regardless of string length.
findings.problem: Lack of tabular grid alignment: Rows use unconstrained flex spacing without table column definitions or headers. When container image names vary in length (e.g., ghcr.io/acme/builder:2026.10 in row 3 vs 45-character image names in rows 1-2), the resource specifications and timestamps shift horizontally across columns, destroying vertical scannability.

findings.fix: Add an explicit neutral/muted token for stopped state (e.g. #64748B) to the brand system, and replace pink #F57AB4 with an accessible red token (e.g. #EF4444) for error states that aligns with the destructive action color.
findings.location: States color tokens in Brand System
findings.problem: Incomplete state palette and low-contrast error token: The brand system palette defines only success (#3DDC97), warning (#FFC857), and error (#F57AB4), completely omitting a token for stopped/inactive states (which appears ad-hoc in c01 and c10). Furthermore, using pink/magenta (#F57AB4) for errors yields poor contrast and breaks developer conventions where errors and destructive operations are red.

findings.fix: Define a first-class semantic token map for light mode in the brand system, ensuring darker, high-contrast equivalents for status colors (e.g., #DC2626 for failed, #166534 for running) that satisfy WCAG AAA for body text and AA for labels.
findings.location: Status labels and table text across light mode
findings.problem: Light mode palette adaptation fails WCAG contrast: In light mode, status labels such as ci-job failed use magenta (#D12771) and stopped uses pale grey (#6B778C), while the palette laboratory (c12) only defines dark mode values without an inverted token mapping. Several text elements fail WCAG AA contrast against the pure white (#FFFFFF) background.

findings.fix: Standardize heading typography across the entire suite: either commit to the monospace slab-serif for all primary titles to reinforce the technical infrastructure identity, or use a refined sans-serif (like Inter/Geist) consistently everywhere.
findings.location: Heading typography and brand font divergence
findings.problem: Brand typography schizophrenia across screens: Screens c01–c06 render view headings ('Workspaces', 'api') and modal titles in a standard sans-serif typeface, whereas c08, c10, c11, and c12 render headings in a distinct slab-serif monospace font. This creates an inconsistent brand identity between app screens and the site/laboratory.

findings.fix: Render all timestamp strings ('Updated 2m ago', etc.) in the design system's monospace font to ensure tabular numeric alignment and adherence to the infrastructure brand constraint.
findings.problem: Timestamps violate monospace direction constraint: Direction guidelines mandate that IDs, image names, and timestamps be set in a monospace face. While IDs and image names are monospace, timestamps ('Updated 2m ago', 'Updated yesterday', '2 min ago') are rendered in proportional sans-serif font.

findings.fix: Remove inline deletion cards from dashboard content containers; always invoke destructive confirmations as centered modal overlays with background scrims (as done in c05/c06).
findings.problem: Destructive confirmation card rendered inline within content card: In c10, 'Delete agent-1?' is rendered as an unmodalized card placed directly beneath the table inside the main card next to the toast notification, rather than as a focused modal dialog with an overlay backdrop scrim. This risks accidental clicks and confounds operational hierarchy.

findings.fix: Establish a strict systemic standard for dialog button placement (e.g. secondary Cancel on left, primary/destructive action on right) and enforce it identically across all dialog variants.
findings.location: Action button ordering in confirmation modal
findings.problem: Inverted button order between confirmation dialogs: In c05/c06, the dialog places [Cancel] on the left and [Delete] on the right. In c10 and c11, the order is reversed: [Delete] is on the left and [Cancel] is on the right. This inconsistency causes muscle-memory errors in critical destructive workflows.

findings.fix: Standardize destructive VM deletion across all views to require typing the resource identifier to confirm deletion, preventing accidental destruction.
findings.problem: Bypassed confirmation typing safety pattern: Screen c05 enforces a safety safeguard requiring the user to type the workspace name ('agent-1') before enabling the Delete action. In c10/c11, this safety safeguard is completely omitted, presenting an unverified one-click destructive button for deleting an isolated VM.

findings.fix: Add a secondary 'Copy' icon/button to the top right of the code snippet container with visual feedback when clicked.
findings.problem: Missing copy affordance for terminal CLI commands: The Connect panel provides CLI commands ('spin ssh api', 'spin snapshot create api...'), but lacks a 'Copy' button or click-to-copy affordance. In developer infrastructure tools (compare ref-beam-apps.png), command snippets must be instantly copyable with a single click.

findings.fix: Replace multi-column tabular layout on mobile viewports (<640px) with stacked responsive cards or list rows with clear key-value hierarchy, preventing text hyphenation and badge wrapping.
findings.problem: Severe table collapse and broken badge wrapping on mobile: In c11, the 4-column desktop table is rendered on a ~360px viewport without responsive reflow. Table headers collide, machine names break mid-word ('agent-' / '1'), status labels wrap to 3 lines ('waiting' / 'for a' / 'host'), and runner badges wrap awkwardly ('runner-' / 'a1').

findings.fix: Provide an overflow/action menu (e.g. kebab icon) on mobile rows containing all operational actions (Stop, View Logs, VS Code, Details), and preserve essential specs in a compact secondary line beneath the workspace name.
findings.location: Workspaces list row actions on mobile
findings.problem: Complete loss of essential operational controls on mobile: The responsive layout in c07 removes the Stop button, View logs button, and VS Code link, and drops all resource specs and image identifiers, leaving only an oversized Open terminal button. A mobile on-call engineer cannot stop runaway instances or diagnose failed jobs.

findings.fix: Style status filters as interactive filter chips/segmented pills with subtle borders and active/selected background states (similar to Beam's tab bar in ref-beam-apps.png).
findings.problem: Status filters lack interactive affordances: The status counters ('Running 2', 'Stopped 1', 'Failed 1') are styled as flat plain text with inline colored symbols, lacking pill containers, borders, or hover/selected affordances. Users cannot distinguish whether these are static summary metrics or clickable filter toggles.

findings.fix: Replace the glossy 3D illustration with a crisp, technical vector schematic (e.g. architecture diagram of sandboxes, snapshots, and diffs) that matches the serious infrastructure branding.
findings.problem: Clashing 3D visual asset: The hero graphic uses a glossy, skeuomorphic 3D blue layered puck/sphere with drop shadows that clashes with the flat, technical, monospace-driven developer aesthetic established across Beam, Boxd, and the Spinbox palette laboratory.

findings.fix: Unify the navigation taxonomy across the entire product into a single consistent structure (adopting the grouped WORK/ADMINISTER structure from c10, as it better matches infrastructure platforms).
findings.problem: Incompatible sidebar information architecture: c10 introduces a categorized sidebar (WORK vs ADMINISTER) with Hosts and Snapshots as primary navigation items, whereas c01 has a flat sidebar with Dashboard, Workspaces, Shared with me, Teams, and Settings. The product lacks a unified navigation architecture.

findings.fix: Change row-level action buttons (Open terminal, Start) to secondary outline or ghost buttons, reserving the filled cyan accent exclusively for the primary view-level call-to-action (New workspace).
findings.problem: Every running row uses a filled bright cyan primary accent button ([Open terminal]) and the stopped row uses filled cyan ([Start]), directly competing with the top-level [New workspace] primary action and violating the brand rule of reserving the solid accent for the single primary action per view.

findings.fix: Standardize row actions into a unified button group or apply consistent secondary outline button styling to 'VS Code' with an icon placeholder matching other row actions.
findings.location: workspace row actions, rightmost item ('VS Code')
findings.problem: 'VS Code' is rendered as plain unstyled text without a button container, border, or icon placeholder, creating an inconsistent action affordance alongside bordered [Stop] and filled [Open terminal] buttons.

findings.fix: Disable the [Delete] button (muted background, disabled cursor, inactive state) until the input text exactly matches the target workspace name 'agent-1'.
findings.problem: The destructive [Delete] button is rendered in an active, fully enabled red state even though the workspace name confirmation input contains an invalid value ('agent') and displays a mismatch error.

findings.fix: Adjust the light mode error/failed token to a deeper crimson/ruby red (e.g., #B91C1C or #DC2626) that achieves at least 4.5:1 contrast against white and light surfaces.
findings.location: status badges and validation text in light mode
findings.problem: The error/failed state color (#F57AB4 pink) and validation text have insufficient contrast against white surfaces (approx. 2.3:1), failing WCAG AA requirements for readable text.

findings.fix: Unify error, failure, and destructive actions under a coherent red family (e.g., crimson/red-600) with dedicated variants for text, surfaces, and active borders.
findings.location: semantic state tokens in palette laboratory
findings.problem: The palette defines error/failed as pink (#F57AB4) while destructive actions use crimson red (#C2304F), splitting failure semantics across two unrelated hues and conflicting with established infrastructure conventions where failure and destructive danger share consistent red semantics.

findings.fix: Stack workspace metadata beneath the name in a multi-line card/row layout and provide an overflow actions menu (...) so operational actions remain accessible on mobile.
findings.problem: The responsive mobile view strips out essential metadata (image repo, CPU/memory/disk specifications, relative update timestamps) and completely omits the Stop, VS Code, and View logs actions, making failed or running workspaces unmanageable on narrow screens.

findings.fix: Replace multi-column table layout on mobile with stacked definition cards, or enable horizontal overflow scrolling (overflow-x: auto) with white-space nowrap on monospace identifiers.
findings.problem: Table columns on narrow viewports lack min-width constraints and horizontal scrolling, causing severe mid-word line breaks and hyphenation across technical IDs and states (agent- / 1, runner- / a1, waiting / for a / host).

findings.fix: Standardize all display headings on the geometric sans-serif typeface used in c01-c04, restricting monospace strictly to code blocks, CLI commands, container image tags, and machine identifiers.
findings.problem: Headlines on documentation and dashboard screens (c08, c09, c10, c11) use a slab-serif typewriter monospace font, conflicting with the clean sans-serif typography used throughout the main app views (c01-c06).

findings.fix: Consolidate metadata into a compact grid or unified specifications panel with inline resource metrics (similar to Boxd's inline resource bars) and remove full-width horizontal divider lines between every field.
findings.problem: Details and Resources are displayed in two sparse, widely separated columns with heavy horizontal rules under every single property, leaving over half of the view as dead space and providing lower density than infrastructure references.

findings.fix: Adopt a single canonical workspaces view pattern across the product: either a unified high-density data table with configurable columns and actions, or the list-row pattern, ensuring host, image, and specs are consistently represented.
findings.problem: Screen c10 introduces a standard table layout with column headers (Name, State, Host, Last snapshot) and a [Refresh] button, contradicting the card-row pattern in c01 which shows image tags, resource specs, and inline action buttons.

findings.fix: Shift surface tokens from deep navy toward neutral or zinc dark tones (e.g., #09090B, #121214, #18181B), reserving blue/cyan purely for interactive focal points.
findings.location: surface tokens and dark mode canvas
findings.problem: All dark mode surfaces (#111827, #172035, #202C47) use heavily saturated blue-navy tones instead of the neutral, low-saturation charcoals seen in reference products like Beam and Boxd, creating visual fatigue and competing with syntax/code.

findings.fix: Remove the outer bordered container enclosing the page; allow the documentation layout to span the full viewport with standard header, persistent sidebar navigation, and dedicated article content area.
findings.problem: The documentation page wraps the header, hero marketing block, and documentation columns inside a single bordered card floating within an outer dark background, creating artificial nesting and cramped reading margins.

findings.fix: Apply a subtle tinted amber background fill (e.g., amber with 10% opacity) and an amber icon indicator to reinforce the warning semantics beyond the 2px left border.
findings.problem: The Caution callout uses an amber left border indicating caution, but retains the neutral dark blue-gray container background, weakening its semantic distinction from standard code blocks.

findings.fix: Convert status counts into interactive filter pills/tabs with consistent badge styling, enabling users to click to filter the list by state.
findings.problem: The inline status count list ('• Running 2  o Stopped 1  ■ Failed 1') uses loose text with miscellaneous symbol characters (•, o, ■) rather than interactive filter chip affordances.

findings.fix: Enclose Open terminal and VS Code into a structured action button group or dropdown menu of access methods, alongside an isolated secondary Stop button.
findings.problem: The detail screen places VS Code as unstyled plain text adjacent to the bordered [Stop] and filled [Open terminal] buttons, without visual grouping or clear distinction between web terminal vs external IDE launcher.

pairs.reason: Neutral near-black surface with a blue primary keeps white button labels readable and leaves the state colours to carry meaning. B's cyan primary buttons have weak label contrast, and its navy surfaces blend together.
The deeper teal-blue primary gives stronger label contrast and ties into the cyan/blue logo. B's royal blue feels like generic SaaS, and its heavier grey-blue nav highlight competes with the content.
Surfaces are clearly separated, and the Connect panel and code block read as distinct layers. B's navy panel and code block nearly merge, and the cyan primary button is low-contrast with its label.
The primary colour is more distinctive and has better contrast, and the pale-blue code block fits the brand. B's royal blue is more generic.

The dialog stands out cleanly against the dimmed neutral background, and the red Delete button is clearly destructive. In B the navy dialog blends into the page, and the teal primaries behind it add a competing hue.
The destructive Delete button is clearly red and the primaries behind the scrim are subdued. The two are close, and A's accent is the more coherent with the brand.
Version b's blue is clearly separate from the green running state and from failed pink. Version a's cyan on a navy ground sits closer to the status hues and blends with the navy surfaces.

Version b's neutral near-black page with blue accent sits closer to the Beam and boxd references. Surfaces and borders separate more clearly. Version a's navy-on-navy layers blur together, and its teal labels and cyan accent look more like a generic SaaS theme.

Version b has a neutral light surface with a single blue accent, and its code blocks read as quiet panels. Version a tints everything blue-grey, and its teal-blue buttons and banner compete with each other.

The state colours (green, amber, pink, grey) are more distinct against neutral black than against navy. The blue primary button, the red Delete and the neutral Cancel form a clear hierarchy. The dialog and toast separate better from the page.

Version a fits the whole table in the narrow width, including the Last snapshot column. Version b clips that column at the right edge. Version a's wrapped state text and hosts are untidy, but nothing is lost.

Version b's palette is neutral with one blue accent. Its accent-text and on-accent roles are separate and deliberate. Its state colours are readable and not neon. In version a, accent-text equals accent and the surface steps are close together.

findings.problem: The image column is centred and not aligned. Image strings start at different x positions on each row (495, 565, 562), and the action columns shift between rows. The list reads as ragged and can't be scanned in columns.
findings.fix: Use a fixed grid with a column header row (Name, State, Image, Resources, Updated, Actions). Left-align every column and right-align the actions.

findings.problem: The state is small monospace text next to a tiny dot or square. It is weaker than the name, and 'stopped' is a hollow ring in muted grey. Failed pink-magenta text has low contrast on black.
findings.fix: Make state a fixed-width badge or label with a distinct shape per state, a readable size and AA contrast. Give failed more weight.

findings.problem: Open terminal is a filled blue primary on every running row. Several identical filled buttons repeat down the list and dilute the hierarchy. VS Code is a bare text link with no affordance. Stop sits at the same weight as Open.
findings.fix: Make the primary action outline or tonal in the list and reserve filled blue for New workspace. Give VS Code a button affordance. Move destructive and stop actions into a row menu, styled as danger.

findings.location: Empty area below the list and the top-right icon buttons
findings.problem: The page has only four rows and the rest is empty. The two top-right buttons carry no labels, so their meaning is unclear. Nothing shows resource totals, an activity feed or last snapshots.
findings.fix: Add a summary strip (running count, total vCPU/RAM) and label the icon buttons or give them tooltips. Use a denser row with the ID visible.

findings.problem: The label column sits in dim grey and the values are plain text. A bordered Connect card is nested inside a bordered page, and its code block is a third layer. The resources and details tables are the same weight as the card. The ID is the only monospace value of note and carries no copy affordance.
findings.fix: Reduce nesting to two surface levels. Add copy buttons on the ID, image and commands. Lift the label contrast to AA.

findings.problem: Open terminal, Stop and VS Code are separate top-right controls with no destructive separation. Delete and Snapshot are absent from the header, so snapshot and diff have no entry point. The tab bar has 7 tabs of equal weight.
findings.fix: Add Snapshot as a primary action next to Open terminal, and a danger-styled Delete in an overflow menu. Show a state badge in the header.

findings.location: Light theme surfaces and nav selection
findings.problem: The light theme has pure white surfaces with hairline grey borders. The active nav pill is very pale, and the page has no tinted layering. Row and header hierarchy come from borders only.
findings.fix: Add an off-white page background with white content surfaces, and give the selected nav item an accent left bar so the selection survives low contrast.

findings.problem: The dialog is good (type-to-confirm, red Delete), but the error text is magenta and small. The Delete button stays active while the name doesn't match. The body copy wraps with a single orphan word ('up.'). The scrim is dark and the dialog has no icon or other cue.
findings.fix: Disable Delete until the name matches. Use a danger text colour at 14px or larger with an icon. Tighten the copy.

findings.problem: Only the desktop layout is shown. The list rows pack eight items into one line with no wrap, truncation or column drop. The 7-tab bar and the two-column tables have no narrow design.
findings.fix: Design a narrow row (name and state on line one, image and resources on line two, actions in a menu). Make the tab bar scroll and stack the tables.

findings.location: Docs site hero and code blocks
findings.problem: The hero headline is a very large monospace face that is hard to read. The cyan brand colour is used for the eyebrows, links, buttons, nav highlight and the banner all at once, so the accent loses its meaning. The Caution block uses a yellow bar that appears nowhere else. The code block is the same navy as the page, so it barely separates.
findings.fix: Set headlines in the proportional face and keep monospace for code and IDs. Limit the accent to links and one primary button. Give code blocks a darker inset surface. Define a callout colour per type.

findings.problem: The site is boxed inside an outer frame with a stray 'THE SITE' label and extra margins. Sidebar items have no section grouping, and the 'On this page' panel is dim and small.
findings.fix: Remove the nested frame. Group the sidebar by section and lift the contrast of the right-hand TOC.

findings.problem: The four-column table is cut off at the right edge, so Last snapshot is clipped. There is no stacked row layout or visible scroll cue.
findings.fix: Below about 480px, turn each row into a stacked item (name and state on the first line, host and snapshot as mono metadata beneath). Alternatively, wrap the table in an overflow container with an edge fade.

findings.problem: The table has no per-row actions. Open terminal, Start, Stop and Delete are missing, so the operational actions the page exists for are not visible. Only a name link exists.
findings.fix: Add a right-aligned actions column with a primary action per state and a quiet overflow menu. Style Delete in the destructive colour only inside the menu or the dialog.

findings.problem: The dialog and the toast are drawn inline under the table with no scrim. They read as page content, and the toast floats beside the dialog.
findings.fix: Render the dialog modally over a scrim. Pin the toast to a corner. Put the destructive button on the right and make the confirmation name the resource in mono.

findings.problem: Every running row carries a large solid blue Open terminal button. The primary-action colour is repeated four times and dominates the list. The ids, state and snapshot time that matter are small.
findings.fix: Make row actions ghost or outline buttons. Keep one solid primary per view (New workspace). Add a mono id and image line to each row.

findings.problem: Two empty square outlines sit beside New workspace with no label, and the filter chips are not visibly interactive.
findings.fix: Give the icon buttons accessible labels and tooltips. Style the filter chips as toggles with a selected state.

findings.problem: The steps between page, surface, raised and overlay are about 4-6 lightness points. Cards and the sidebar blend into the page and rely on thin borders.
findings.fix: Widen the surface steps, or make the border token consistently visible. Check each pairing against 1.2:1 or better.

findings.problem: The grey of stopped, the waiting amber and the failed pink are close in lightness on dark. Mono 11-12px labels are small, so the shapes carry most of the distinction.
findings.fix: Use larger state glyphs and 13px labels. Add a distinct stopped glyph shape and show the state pill on a surface to check contrast.

findings.problem: A large mono headline and the whole docs frame sit inside a bordered box labelled THE SITE. The 3D logo illustration clashes with the flat, restrained system.
findings.fix: Use a flatter or monochrome mark in the hero, or shrink it. Drop the nested frame outside the lab page.

findings.problem: Code blocks and the caution box share the same fill. The comparison table has no header weight and its rule lines are weak, so the content structure is flat.
findings.fix: Give code a recessed surface and the caution a tinted warning background. Make the table header a mono small-caps row with a stronger bottom rule.

findings.problem: The navigation has only a few items. Its selected state is a faint blue wash with no edge marker. The section labels WORK and ADMINISTER are tiny and low-contrast.
findings.fix: Add a 2px accent edge to the selected item and raise the label contrast. Add counts such as Workspaces 4.

findings.problem: Name links are blue and underlined on every row, so the column is noisy. Host chips and plain timestamps are inconsistent: hosts are mono but timestamps are proportional.
findings.fix: Show names as bold text, underlined on hover only. Set timestamps and ids in mono across the table.

findings.problem: The banner is a saturated blue-lavender strip. The grey code blocks and the page are close in tone, so the light theme feels flat next to the dark one.
findings.fix: Use a neutral info banner with a left rule. Add a border to the code surfaces and raise the contrast of the muted text.

pairs.reason: The navy-and-cyan system feels more specific to Spinbox and gives operational actions a clearer, less generic presence.
The restrained cyan action color is more distinctive and less visually heavy than saturated blue on the light surface.
The navy content surface and cyan primary action create a more coherent infrastructure-console identity.
Cyan provides clearer continuity with the dark mode and product mark while preserving the sparse data layout.
The navy modal better belongs to the application shell and maintains a deliberate destructive-action hierarchy.
The two light confirmation dialogs are visually indistinguishable at the supplied scale.
The navy surface system gives the compact workspace list clearer structure and a more deliberate infrastructure-console identity.
The dark documentation page has stronger brand cohesion, with cyan used consistently to guide attention without changing the information architecture.
The teal primary action and pale teal contextual surfaces create a clearer, more distinctive light-mode system.
The dashboard’s navy surfaces, selected navigation treatment, and cyan primary action form a more coherent operational UI.
It preserves all table columns at the narrow viewport; version b clips essential table content horizontally.
The palette is more internally coherent and gives Spinbox a distinctive cyan-on-navy identity suited to the product.

findings.problem: Rows rely on alignment alone; there are no column labels, so image, resources, freshness, and actions take a moment to parse.
findings.fix: Add a compact desktop table header or persistent field labels aligned to the existing columns.

findings.problem: Primary terminal actions repeat at full visual weight for every running row, making the list action-heavy before the user has evaluated the workspaces.
findings.fix: Keep one strong row action, but place secondary actions such as Stop and VS Code in an overflow or quieter inline action group.

findings.problem: The top-right unlabeled controls are indistinguishable from the supplied icon placeholders and have no visible purpose.
findings.fix: Use visible labels, tooltips with recognizable non-placeholder icons, or remove controls that are not essential at list level.

findings.problem: The large empty horizontal gap between the left identity block and right actions weakens the relationship between the workspace state and its controls.
findings.fix: Use a bounded header grid that groups title/state with actions while preserving room for long image identifiers.

findings.problem: The code surface is close in value to the surrounding panel and competes weakly with the command text.
findings.fix: Increase the code-panel tonal separation slightly while retaining its restrained border.

findings.problem: Labels and values have similar visual weight, making resource facts and metadata slower to scan in light mode.
findings.fix: Reduce label contrast/weight modestly and reserve stronger text for values, IDs, and actionable links.

findings.problem: The Delete button is visually active despite an explicitly invalid confirmation value, which makes the destructive state ambiguous.
findings.fix: Disable Delete until the exact name matches and show the enabled destructive state only after validation succeeds.

findings.problem: The recovery-window sentence is grammatically unclear: “until its days are up.”
findings.fix: State the retention period explicitly, for example “You can restore it from Trash for 30 days.”

findings.problem: The gray backdrop preserves too much background contrast, so the destructive confirmation does not isolate the task as strongly as the dark-mode dialog.
findings.fix: Use a slightly darker neutral overlay and ensure dialog elevation is carried by surface contrast and border rather than a broad shadow alone.

findings.problem: The sidebar has substantial unused vertical space while Settings and account information are isolated at the bottom without a clear grouping hierarchy.
findings.fix: Introduce explicit lower-nav grouping and compact the account/settings region into a consistent footer section.

findings.problem: “offline Change” runs together, obscuring that Change is an action rather than part of the value.
findings.fix: Separate the status value and action with spacing and use a distinct link treatment.

findings.problem: The three-column documentation frame leaves the article column relatively narrow while the right table of contents has little content.
findings.fix: Allow the article column to expand when the right rail is sparse, or collapse the page TOC into the article header at this viewport.

findings.problem: The preferred system does not have a robust narrow-table pattern: the alternate version visibly clips the last-snapshot column, while the selected version compresses status text into awkward multi-line fragments.
findings.fix: At this breakpoint replace table rows with labeled stacked records, or retain only Name and State and move host/snapshot into row detail.

findings.problem: The destructive confirmation looks like another inline card beneath the table and competes with a nearby success toast; it lacks strong interaction priority for an irreversible operational action.
findings.fix: Use a focused dialog with backdrop and explicit keyboard focus, or attach an inline danger panel directly to the selected agent row.

findings.problem: An inline-code/control fragment is visibly clipped at the right edge after the Restore text.
findings.fix: Remove the overflowing element or let the inline content wrap naturally within the content column.

findings.problem: The same clipped inline fragment appears in light mode, so the issue is systemic rather than theme-specific.
findings.fix: Apply the same responsive inline-content sizing and wrapping rule in both themes.

findings.problem: Running entries expose only the Open terminal action, while stopped and failed entries lack equally visible contextual next actions or explanation.
findings.fix: Provide a compact per-row action menu and state-appropriate primary action, such as Start for stopped and View failure for failed.

findings.problem: The label token is shown as a highly saturated cyan block, making it read like an accent/action color instead of a quiet metadata role.
findings.fix: Reserve cyan for interactive emphasis and use a subdued but AA-compliant blue-gray token for labels and secondary metadata.

findings.problem: The table is dense and readable, but its row affordance is mostly limited to linked names; operational actions are not discoverable at scan speed.
findings.fix: Expose a compact trailing action menu per row with Open, snapshot, stop/start, and delete actions appropriate to state.

pairs.reason: Neutral dark slate surfaces provide higher text contrast and professional restraint, avoiding version b's oversaturated cyan glow and blue color-cast that fatigues the eyes.
Royal blue accent offers superior contrast and clear visual separation from green running indicators, whereas version a's teal accent visually clashes and competes with running states.
Neutral slate background and crisp royal blue accent maximize legibility for dense technical specs and terminal commands without distracting cyan glare.
Royal blue delivers robust WCAG-compliant contrast for text links and primary actions on light surfaces, whereas version a's teal text suffers from reduced legibility.
Neutral modal surface and overlay ensure clear elevation and sharp contrast for the destructive red action and inline validation errors without navy tinting contamination.
Cohesive light palette where background actions recede predictably and the destructive confirmation action commands immediate, unambiguous visual attention.

findings.fix: Introduce a persistent tabular header row (Name, Status, Image, Specs, Updated, Actions) with subtle muted text, enabling sorting on compute specs and last updated time.
findings.location: Workspace list header above row items
findings.problem: The workspaces list lacks table column headers, making scanning dense infrastructure specs (CPU, memory, storage) and alignment ambiguous across variable-length rows.

findings.fix: Convert status counters into interactive filter pills with clear badge borders and active toggle states to allow one-click filtering by state.
findings.location: Status counter row next to search input
findings.problem: Status counts (Running 2, Stopped 1, Failed 1) appear as passive text without interactive filter affordances.

findings.fix: Standardize the action column layout with a fixed right-aligned slot for primary lifecycle action (Open terminal / Start / View logs) followed by a secondary action (Stop) and an overflow menu.
findings.location: Row action button groups on workspace list items
findings.problem: Inconsistent action button widths and shifting positions between running, stopped, and failed rows break vertical scanning and muscle memory.

findings.fix: Add an explicit header action group including a primary 'Create Snapshot' button and a destructive 'Delete' button with standard confirmation modal triggers.
findings.problem: The workspace detail header omits lifecycle actions for Snapshot and Delete, which are top user workflows for sandbox VM management.

findings.fix: Compact the definition list into a structured two-column key-value grid with fixed-width label columns (e.g. 120px) to prevent excessive whitespace gaps.
findings.problem: Excessive horizontal gap between keys and values across wide dividers forces horizontal eye-tracking across empty space.

findings.fix: Add a dedicated one-click 'Copy' button in the upper-right corner of the code block container with visual feedback on click.
findings.problem: The CLI connection snippet lacks a one-click copy affordance for terminal commands.

findings.fix: Add numerical count badges to relevant tabs (e.g. Snapshots (3)) and an alert indicator badge on Logs when a workspace failure occurs.
findings.problem: Subnavigation tabs lack contextual badges or operational state indicators for fast status triage.

findings.fix: Enforce a strict monospace font stack across image registries and tags, with subdued coloring for registry prefixes to highlight container tags.
findings.problem: Container image paths and digests blend with standard sans-serif text, reducing scannability for DevOps engineers.

findings.fix: Highlight the required confirmation string in a bold monospace badge inside the helper text and enable autofocus on the confirmation input.
findings.problem: Confirmation prompt does not highlight the target workspace name within the instruction sentence, increasing cognitive load before typing.

findings.fix: Add an inline action link (e.g. 'View snapshot') and a dismiss button with standard spacing from the viewport edge.
findings.problem: Toast notification lacks an action link to view the published snapshot and provides no dismiss affordance.

pairs.reason: The neutral near-black list shows one quiet action per row plus an overflow menu, so state and image IDs read first. The navy and cyan version repeats filled cyan Open terminal buttons in every row, and the accent competes with the state dots.

Light mode keeps the same calm structure: one tonal action per row and a row menu. The other version has a saturated blue fill on every row and three buttons across each row, which is heavier than the data.

The detail header has a clear action hierarchy: Stop, a single primary Open terminal, and an overflow menu. The neutral surfaces separate the nav, the tables and the Connect panel better than navy on navy.

The header has one primary button, a secondary Stop and an overflow menu, with calm grey surfaces. The other version shows three equal-weight buttons, including VS Code as bare text, so the primary action is less clear.

The neutral dark dialog is a distinct raised surface over a dimmed list. The red Delete is the only saturated element, so the destructive action reads clearly. The navy version blends the modal into the page.

The white dialog on a dimmed grey page has a clear tonal Cancel and a red Delete. The other version's slate backdrop with a blue-tinted page looks muddier and mixes the blue accent into the dimmed rows.

Rows use quiet secondary buttons, a contextual 'View logs' action for the failed row and an overflow menu. Only 'New workspace' is filled, so the one primary action stands out. Version a fills every row with a saturated cyan button, which buries state and the primary action.
The neutral near-black surfaces and the calmer blue accent are closer to the Beam and boxd consoles. The cyan on navy in version a is more saturated, and the surfaces blend into each other.

The neutral gray surfaces for code blocks and callouts are more restrained and keep the accent for links and the selected item. Version b tints everything blue, so the surfaces blend. The difference is small.

The neutral dark surface and the selected nav row without a cyan wash keep the accent restrained. The dialog puts Cancel first and the red Delete last, the conventional order, and its sans title matches the rest of the UI.

The dialog title is sans-serif and the buttons are right-aligned with Cancel before the red Delete, as on desktop. The surfaces are neutral. In version a the destructive button comes first on the left, which makes a mis-tap more likely.

The palette is neutral and restrained. accent-text is a distinct lighter tone, and the labels are muted rather than neon cyan. The on-accent white-on-blue pairing also looks more deliberate than the identical accent and accent-text values in version b.

findings.problem: The image column floats with no fixed column. Its left edge shifts from row to row (v2026 rows start at about x=545, the builder row at 550, notes at 555), and the resource and updated columns shift with it. The grid looks ragged and is hard to scan.
findings.fix: Use a real table or grid with fixed column tracks for name/state, image, resources, updated and action, and right-align the numeric columns.

findings.problem: The state label is small monospace text at low contrast, with only a tiny dot or square marker. Failed pink and running green are dim on black, so state, which is the main fact in the list, is the weakest element in the row.
findings.fix: Raise state text to AA-plus contrast, use a larger 8–10px glyph with a distinct shape per state, and consider a state column or a subtle row tint for failed.

findings.problem: Stop and Delete are hidden in the … menu and VS Code is gone from the row. The only visible action is a neutral grey button, and nothing in the row signals a destructive path. The tertiary actions have no visible entry point.
findings.fix: Keep Open terminal as the one primary action, expose VS Code in the menu with labels, and set destructive menu items off in a red-toned group at the bottom.

findings.problem: Stop, an operational action that interrupts a running VM, sits first, next to the primary button, in the same neutral style as Change size. Open terminal is a mid-blue fill with modest contrast against the black page.
findings.fix: Order the actions primary first, give Stop a distinct caution treatment or move it into the menu, and give the accent button a stronger fill and text contrast.

findings.location: Details and Resources tables, Connect panel
findings.problem: Detail rows have equal weight. ID, Image, Saved and URL labels, values and links are all one size, and the long Saved sentence breaks the key-value rhythm. The Resources table is a second equal-weight block and the page leaves its lower half empty. The detail has little operational context such as a snapshot or diff summary.
findings.fix: Put state, uptime and last snapshot in a header strip, add copy buttons on IDs and the image, and place snapshots and diff above the fold with a compact timeline.

findings.problem: The product has no top bar or workspace context. Navigation, search, status and account all sit in the left rail, and there are no breadcrumbs or org name. Compared with boxd and Beam, global state and the environment are invisible.
findings.fix: Add a slim top bar with account or org, the region/AWS account, and a health or version indicator; keep the rail for navigation only.

findings.problem: Delete is red and enabled while the typed name does not match, with the error shown below. The destructive action gives no disabled state. The pink error text is small and low in contrast on the dark panel. The dialog does not repeat any identifying facts such as the workspace ID or snapshot count.
findings.fix: Disable Delete until the name matches, make the error text AA contrast with an icon, and show the workspace ID and the size of what is lost.

findings.problem: In light mode the grey tonal buttons, grey code block and grey row-hover fills are close in value to the page, so the buttons look disabled. The pale selected nav item and the grey Cancel are nearly identical.
findings.fix: Give buttons a defined 1px border and a darker fill than the surface, and use a clearer selected state in the nav, such as an accent bar.

findings.location: Filter bar: input and state counts
findings.problem: The Running, Stopped and Failed counts look like legend text, not filters. They have no active or hover affordance, and the search input has a faint border and weak contrast.
findings.fix: Make them toggle chips with a pressed state and counts in tabular monospace, and give the input a visible border and a focus ring.

findings.problem: Only the desktop viewport is shown. The 240px sidebar and the one-line rows (name, long image path, resources, updated, action) have no visible collapsed or stacked treatment, so narrow widths are undesigned.
findings.fix: Define a rail that collapses to icons, and a row layout that stacks the image and resources under the name below about 900px, with truncation and copy for the image.

findings.problem: The bottom-right toast mixes a small mono 'done' label with a sans/mono sentence ('Snapshot clean published') and has no dismiss control or link to the snapshot.
findings.fix: Use one type style for the message, link to the snapshot or its diff, and add a dismiss button.

findings.problem: Neutral black with a flat blue accent and small grey type is clean but close to generic dashboard styling. The brand's layered blue/cyan identity shows only in the logo, so the surfaces, borders and corners say little about Spinbox.
findings.fix: Take a distinctive element from the brand, such as a layered-disc motif for snapshot or diff states, a signature accent tone, or tighter squared corners, and apply it to the selected nav, tabs and snapshot timeline.

findings.problem: State is a small coloured dot or shape plus a monospace word. Nothing else in the row carries it: there are no row actions, and the failed and waiting rows look like the others. findings.problem: The dialog sits inline below the table, with no scrim and no focus isolation, so it reads as a content card. The copy says 'until its days are up' with no number. The workspace name is not set in monospace, and nothing makes the user confirm the target.
findings.fix: Render it as a modal over a scrim, with a concrete retention period and the name in a mono chip. Keep Delete in the destructive red, placed last.

findings.problem: The selected item is only a faint background and the sidebar is the same colour as the content. Navigation, content and detail blur together. There is no user, org or search area like those in Beam and boxd.
findings.fix: Give the sidebar its own surface and a 2px accent marker on the selected item. Add a footer with the user, org and status.

findings.location: Toast and dialog in one row
findings.problem: The toast is placed beside the dialog in the document flow. It looks like a content block, and its left edge doesn't line up with anything.
findings.fix: Fix the toast to a corner overlay with consistent elevation.

findings.problem: Two unlabeled square controls sit next to the primary button. There are no ID, image or time metadata under the names. The list leaves roughly half the screen empty. The state chips (Running 2, and so on) look like filters but give no sign that they are.
findings.fix: Add a second line of monospace image and ID plus the last snapshot time to each row. Make the state chips obviously filter toggles with a selected style.

findings.problem: The table is squeezed rather than redesigned. Host values wrap to 'runner-/a1', 'agent-/1' breaks across two lines, and the state text wraps. The ID in the first column is unreadable.
findings.fix: On narrow screens, switch to stacked rows with name and state on the first line and host and snapshot as a mono second line, or scroll horizontally with a sticky name column.

findings.problem: The mark's ground shadow turns into a pale ring in the neutral dark theme and looks pasted on. The headline is a very large monospace in a wide measure. The hero takes about 400px of height before any docs content appears.
findings.fix: Make the shadow transparent or tone it to the surface. Cap the headline size and measure, and tighten the vertical padding.

findings.problem: The caution callout, the code blocks and the table sit on near-identical surfaces. The table has no container, and it touches the callout above it with no spacing. The warning is separated only by a thin amber bar.
findings.fix: Give callouts their own tint and an icon or shape. Add a margin above the table and give it a header surface.

findings.problem: The warning, error and success hues are bright pastels (pink #F286C2 for failed) and are close in luminance. Failed pink reads as a soft, friendly colour rather than an error. The red destructive colour and the pink error colour differ, so failure and deletion use two different reds.
findings.fix: Use a true red for error that shares a family with destructive. Reserve the state colours for chips with a shape and a label.

findings.problem: The page, surface, raised and overlay steps are only a few lightness points apart (#0E1013 to #262B32). In the app, nested areas such as cards, code and the dialog barely separate and rely on a hairline border.
findings.fix: Widen the steps between the surface layers, or use consistently stronger borders between layers.

findings.problem: The sidebar selected-item tint, the banner and the code blocks use similar pale blue-grey. The on-this-page links are low contrast against white. The mono eyebrow labels are dark blue and look different from the dark theme's tones.
findings.fix: Darken the muted text to reach AA. Differentiate the banner from the code surfaces.

findings.problem: Action buttons differ in width per row ('Open terminal', 'View logs', 'Start'), so their left edges are ragged. The overflow dots have no visible hit area. Nothing shows where delete lives.
findings.fix: Use a fixed action column width and a bordered 32px overflow button that holds Delete in red.

The two light-mode documentation renderings are visually indistinguishable.
The selected navigation, confirmation surface, and success toast use the same restrained dark-blue system, giving the operational view stronger cohesion.
The destructive confirmation gives Delete clear priority while retaining a clean, accessible mobile action layout.
