findings.problem: Running rows expose Open terminal, Stop, and VS Code as three similarly prominent adjacent actions, making quick scanning harder in the densest part of the product.
findings.fix: Keep Open terminal as the sole visible primary action; move Stop and VS Code into a consistent overflow or compact secondary action pattern.

findings.problem: Two unlabeled square controls appear before New workspace without visible meaning, creating ambiguity in the page’s primary control area.
findings.fix: Use recognizable icons with tooltips and active-state labels, or replace them with text controls when their meaning is important.

findings.problem: The cyan filled operational buttons are much more visually dominant than row names and states, so the table reads as a field of actions rather than a workspace inventory.
findings.fix: Reserve filled accent treatment for the page-level creation action; use quieter outlined or text actions at row level, retaining color for status.

findings.problem: Stop is visually presented as an ordinary gray secondary control with no caution signal despite being a disruptive operational action.
findings.fix: Use a warning-toned outline or an explicit pause/stop semantic treatment while keeping terminal access as the primary action.

findings.problem: The two-column key/value layout has substantial unused horizontal space while long image identifiers remain visually dense.
findings.fix: Constrain each definition list to a readable max width and give identifier values a dedicated flexible column with truncation/copy affordance.

findings.problem: The pale blue-gray code surface is noticeably stronger than the surrounding neutral panels and does not map cleanly to the dark-mode code treatment.
findings.fix: Define a shared code-surface token for both themes with a subtler neutral tint and distinct border, preserving monospace contrast.

findings.problem: Delete remains fully enabled while the entered workspace name is visibly invalid, weakening the confirmation safeguard.
findings.fix: Disable Delete until the exact name matches and provide the mismatch message as the blocking explanation.

findings.problem: The dialog’s charcoal surface is close to the page canvas, so its containment relies heavily on a thin border.
findings.fix: Increase modal elevation through a slightly lighter elevated surface and a softer, broader shadow while maintaining the restrained console palette.

findings.problem: Cancel is filled gray in light mode whereas it is outlined in the preferred dark treatment, producing inconsistent secondary-button hierarchy across themes.
findings.fix: Standardize Cancel as an outlined secondary action in both themes; reserve filled treatments for the destructive confirmation.

findings.problem: Rows omit column labels and place state, action, and overflow controls in a compressed horizontal pattern; scanning many workspaces will become ambiguous as metadata grows.
findings.fix: Use a compact stacked row on narrow screens: workspace and state first, contextual metadata below, then actions in a dedicated trailing or expanded action region.

findings.problem: The toast is visually isolated at the very bottom with substantial unused space above it, making it feel disconnected from the snapshot action it confirms.
findings.fix: Anchor transient feedback nearer the affected action or use a standard viewport corner with consistent offsets.

findings.problem: The central prose column is constrained while the right table-of-contents column has large unused space, creating an inefficient reading layout.
findings.fix: Widen the article column modestly or make the right rail sticky and narrower so line lengths and available width are better balanced.

findings.problem: The large illustration competes slightly with the already dominant multi-line monospace headline.
findings.fix: Reduce illustration scale or lower its contrast so the product proposition remains the undisputed hero focal point.

findings.problem: The confirmation is embedded beneath the table rather than blocking or clearly overlaying the destructive decision context, so it can be mistaken for another dashboard card.
findings.fix: Present deletion in a modal/dialog layer with a focused title, clear target name, and keyboard focus management; retain the inline result only after confirmation.

findings.problem: Search, New workspace, and Refresh have similar visual weight despite distinctly different roles.
findings.fix: Keep New workspace primary, soften Refresh to tertiary styling, and let the search field carry its input affordance without competing borders.

findings.problem: The dialog uses a desktop-card treatment inside the content flow, which makes it easy to scroll past and leaves its relationship to the selected workspace unclear.
findings.fix: Use a responsive modal or bottom sheet with an explicit selected-workspace reference and a persistent decision area.

findings.problem: Accent and accent-text are the same cyan value, obscuring the distinction between an action fill and text placed on that fill.
findings.fix: Define separate tokens: an accessible dark foreground for text/icons on cyan actions and a cyan token for links or action surfaces as appropriate.

findings.problem: The bright teal label token has a stronger visual pull than ordinary content hierarchy and risks being overused as decorative emphasis.
findings.fix: Reserve the label token for small metadata/eyebrows and add a muted label variant for routine secondary metadata.

pairs.reason: Neutral dark background and restrained secondary row actions with an overflow menu establish clear visual hierarchy, avoiding the visual noise of repetitive bright cyan buttons.
Disciplined hierarchy with an authoritative dark primary CTA and subdued row actions with overflow menus, avoiding repetitive saturated teal buttons across the list.
Neutral charcoal surface provides superior contrast and elevates 'Open terminal' as the primary action alongside an overflow menu for full lifecycle management.
Clear action hierarchy prioritizing 'Open terminal' over secondary controls, complemented by an overflow menu for operational completeness.
High-contrast neutral dark card elevates cleanly above the backdrop scrim without bright cyan background buttons distracting from the destructive confirmation.
Calm light-mode backdrop dimming and restrained table rows focus complete user attention on the destructive deletion confirmation.

findings.fix: Add a subtle low-contrast table header row with column labels and sort triggers.

findings.problem: Status counts ('Running 2', 'Stopped 1', 'Failed 1') lack interactive filter affordances or an 'All' toggle option.

findings.problem: Destructive/interruptive 'Stop' button is placed directly adjacent to primary CTA 'Open terminal', risking accidental shutdown.

findings.fix: Render uncommitted disk writes with an amber warning badge and an inline 'Publish snapshot' action button.

findings.fix: Move snapshot count to Details metadata or directly into the Snapshots tab header.
findings.problem: Listing 'Snapshots: 3' under hardware 'Resources' conflates compute provisioning (CPU, RAM, Disk) with point-in-time backup history.

findings.fix: Add a copy-to-clipboard button in the upper-right corner of the code block with visual feedback on copy.
findings.problem: The CLI connection command block lacks a dedicated one-click copy button.

findings.fix: Use a semantic status badge with an indicator dot (e.g. neutral/muted for offline, green for online) to indicate network state.
findings.problem: Network 'offline' state is rendered in unstyled plain text, failing to communicate network connectivity semantics.

findings.fix: Add helper text or modal validation clarifying that instance resizing requires a stop/restart cycle.
findings.problem: The 'Change size' button does not indicate whether resizing requires the VM to be stopped, risking unexpected disruption.

findings.fix: Add a dismiss trigger and a direct link to view the snapshot in the Snapshots tab.
findings.problem: The snapshot completion toast ('• done Snapshot clean published') lacks a dismiss button and an actionable link to inspect the snapshot.

findings.fix: Clearly delineate global command palette search from local table filtering using distinct styling and keyboard affordances.
findings.problem: Global search ('Search ⌘K') in the sidebar sits directly beside the local table filter ('Name or image'), creating ambiguous search scoping.

findings.fix: Brighten the validation message color to high-contrast rose/amber to satisfy WCAG AAA on dark surfaces.
findings.problem: The validation error text ('The name does not match agent-1.') has marginal contrast against the dark modal surface.

findings.fix: Reflow the mobile table into a single-column stacked card list layout (similar to s01-b) where machine name, state badge, host, and last snapshot occupy structured vertical rows rather than rigid table columns.
findings.location: Workspaces data table columns (Name, State, Host)
findings.problem: On narrow mobile viewports, the desktop 4-column data table is retained without reflowing or horizontal scrolling, causing table cells to compress and text to break awkwardly across hyphenated fragments (e.g. 'agent-' / '1', 'runner-' / 'a1', and 'waiting' / '◆ for a' / 'host').

findings.fix: Render destructive confirmation dialogs inside a centered modal overlay with a semi-transparent dark backdrop scrim that traps focus and clearly separates modal interaction from page content.
findings.problem: The destructive confirmation dialog is rendered as an un-anchored inline card directly below the table rows rather than an overlay modal with a backdrop scrim, creating layout confusion and competing with table content.

findings.fix: Add a compact secondary metadata row underneath each workspace name in monospace font (e.g. 'runner-a1 · 2 min ago') before the action button group.
findings.problem: In mobile list view (s01-b), machine metadata such as assigned host (runner-a1), hardware specs, and last snapshot timestamp are completely missing, forcing users to navigate blindly without knowing machine context.

findings.fix: Reserve the monospaced typeface strictly for code blocks, terminal snippets, IDs, and runner names; use a refined, geometric or grotesque sans-serif with tighter tracking for display and page titles.
findings.location: Hero display headline ('A virtual machine per workspace. A snapshot before, a diff after.')
findings.problem: Using a wide slab/monospaced typewriter typeface for large display headlines creates uneven typographic color, wide tracking gaps, and awkward visual rhythm on marketing and documentation headers.

findings.fix: Add an 'Actions' column on desktop rows with quick-action buttons (Terminal/Start) and a three-dots menu for secondary actions (Snapshot, Diff, Delete), matching the affordances provided in the mobile view (s01-b).
findings.location: Workspaces table header and row action area
findings.problem: The desktop workspaces table lacks direct operational action triggers (such as Terminal, Start/Stop, Snapshot, or overflow '...') on the rows themselves; actions only appear when selecting or through contextual modals.

findings.fix: Add a 3px semantic border accent (e.g., border-left: 3px solid #4CC38A) matching the status color of the notification.
findings.problem: On mobile, the toast notification lacks a semantic status color accent on its container border, relying solely on a small green dot icon which reduces at-a-glance state feedback.

findings.fix: Give the warning banner a distinct border and slightly warmer warning tint (#E3B04B at 10% opacity) or subtle amber left accent line to indicate experimental/prerelease status clearly.
findings.location: Documentation site top banner ('Spinbox is experimental...')
findings.problem: The experimental warning banner spans the full width with a low-contrast dark cyan fill that visually merges into the header rather than appearing as a distinct system callout.

findings.fix: Add a keyboard shortcut badge (e.g. '⌘K') inside the search input and provide quick filter chips for common workspace states (Running, Stopped, Failed).
findings.problem: The search bar lacks a keyboard shortcut affordance (e.g. '⌘K' or '/'), search scope indicator, or quick filters, lagging behind developer console standards set by Beam and boxd.

findings.fix: Align the palette tokens in s06 with the neutral dark architecture from s06-a: set surface-page to #0E1013, primary accent to #1B7DB4, on-accent to #FFFFFF, and remove saturated blue tints from neutral surfaces.

findings.problem: The image column is centred or floats at an inconsistent x between rows (ci-job and notes are offset from api). Long GHCR names also dominate the row, so name and state get less weight than the image.

findings.problem: Stop and Delete are hidden in the ⋯ menu, so the destructive operation has no visible affordance and the row has no visible keyboard route to it. Stop is also missing from the list that the detail page offers.

findings.problem: The filter chips use dot, ring and square shapes at very small size. Counts are set in tiny monospace, and the chips do not look clickable. The stopped ring is low contrast.
findings.fix: Make the chips real toggle buttons with a border and selected state, and use larger tabular counts. Raise the contrast of the stopped glyph and text.

findings.problem: Open terminal sits on the right next to Stop and an unlabeled ⋯. VS Code, a top workflow, has dropped out of the detail header. Stop is a neutral button and does not signal that it changes state.
findings.fix: Show Open terminal and VS Code as the primary group. Put Stop in its own operational group, and move Delete into a clearly destructive section.

findings.problem: The Details and Resources tables look alike and are separated only by hairlines. The empty lower half of the page has no snapshot or diff summary, even though that is the product's core feature.
findings.fix: Add a snapshots panel with a diff link and a state timeline. Tint or inset the code block as a CLI surface and add a copy button.

findings.problem: The 'running' label is tiny green monospace on charcoal, with a 12px dot. The ID and image line under the title is dim.

findings.problem: The scrim is only slightly darker than the page, and the dialog is barely lifted. The danger message is small pink text on charcoal, and the red Delete is enabled while the name field is invalid.

findings.problem: The error text is dim magenta at about 12px and the dialog has no destructive framing. The red Delete is the same visual weight as the primary blue.
findings.fix: Add a danger icon and heading. Darken the error colour to AA+ and keep red reserved for destructive actions only.

findings.problem: The light theme has near-white surfaces with hairline borders, and the selected sidebar item is a pale grey block. Page, sidebar, rows and cards barely separate.
findings.fix: Add a slightly tinted page background against white content surfaces. Give the active nav item an accent edge or stronger fill.

findings.problem: The docs site is navy with a saturated cyan accent, a glossy 3D logo and a huge monospace headline, and it is wrapped in a boxed frame with a 'THE SITE' label. It reads as a different brand from the neutral app.

findings.problem: Cyan-filled buttons repeat on every row, so the accent loses meaning and is no longer a signal. The navy surfaces are also close in value to the borders.

findings.problem: No narrow or mobile layout is shown. The fixed 240px sidebar and wide row grid have no visible collapse, and rows with long image names would overflow.

findings.problem: Each row shows only a name, a state and one button. There is no image, host or time, so it is far less dense than boxd's machine row.

findings.problem: The dialog is an inline card under the table with no scrim. Delete is placed first and touches Cancel, nothing shows what is destroyed, and the body text is low-contrast.

findings.problem: Every name is an underlined link, so the first column is noisy. The table has no actions column, no row hover or selection state, and the waiting diamond is tiny.

findings.problem: The desktop table is shrunk instead of redesigned. Host chips break mid-word (runner-/a1), the waiting state wraps onto three lines and the header wraps.

findings.fix: Increase non-color differentiation consistently with clearer state icons/badges and ensure muted stopped text meets the same contrast standard in both themes.

findings.problem: Every row exposes an unlabeled ellipsis control, but its menu purpose and available actions are not discoverable from the list.
findings.fix: Use a recognizable kebab affordance with an accessible label and tooltip; reserve it for less-common actions while keeping state-appropriate primary actions visible.

findings.problem: The failed row has only “View logs,” whereas running and stopped rows expose immediate state-changing actions; recovery remains unclear from this primary operational view.
findings.fix: Include the most likely recovery action, such as Retry or Restart, alongside View logs when that action is available.

findings.location: Documentation article, end of introductory paragraph
findings.problem: A small clipped rectangular element appears directly after “disk back;”, reading as a rendering or overflow defect.
findings.fix: Remove the clipped artifact or render its intended control/content fully with a clear accessible label.

findings.problem: The main article is comparatively narrow while the right “On this page” rail has very little content, producing substantial unused space in a dense technical document.
findings.fix: Collapse the right rail when it has only a few anchors, or allocate more width to the reading and code column.

findings.problem: The confirmation is embedded below the table rather than presented as a modal or clearly localized row state, making it easy to lose the target context in a larger workspace list.
findings.fix: Use a modal/dialog with the workspace name and irreversible-effects summary, or anchor an inline confirmation directly to the selected row.

findings.problem: The four-column table compresses host IDs and wraps the waiting status into multiple lines, weakening fast status scanning.
findings.fix: At this breakpoint switch each workspace to a compact stacked row: name/state first, then host and snapshot metadata.

findings.problem: Token swatches show names and hex values but do not communicate intended foreground/background pairings or contrast status, despite the stated AA requirement.
findings.fix: Add approved text-pairing examples and a visible WCAG contrast result to each relevant surface and action token.

findings.problem: The heavy monospace treatment is used broadly for display headings and labels, making hierarchy feel somewhat mechanical rather than selectively emphasizing identifiers and operational data.
findings.fix: Keep monospace for IDs, commands, timestamps, and token names; use a complementary highly legible UI face for navigation and explanatory prose.
